coverageNote: Enumeration from disk matched the expected 5 units / 33 files exactly. Units: the domain directory itself (education-lessons-mentorship-index.md + -cx.md + the 7 loose leaf features 06.05-06.11, 9 files), 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery (6 files), 06.02-teacher-discovery-profiles-trials (6), 06.03-curriculum-assignments-practice (7), 06.04-course-marketplace-authoring (5). Every file was read in full; no sampling. Dimension 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A on every unit: constraints live in meta/constraints.md and competitive analysis in meta/competitive-landscape.md, neither of which is in scope for a domain sub-tree. Dimension 5 (Success Measurability) is scored only on the domain unit, where the domain index carries an explicit success-measure open question (Q-08); it is N/A on the four sub-domain units, which state no metrics and are not the layer where metrics belong. findings.claim: Two files settle a both-parties-no-show in directly opposite ways, and the file that defers points at a row the other file marks RESOLVED. 06.01.02 holds the credit in limbo pending '06.01.03's rule (their Q-03)'; 06.01.03's Q-03 is struck through as RESOLVED and its edge table returns the credit.
findings.evidence: 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:223 — '| 35 | Both parties no-show | The ledger will not burn without a resolved earning event. The credit sits in **limbo**, un-consumed and un-returned, pending 06.01.03's rule (their Q-03). ... | Both: "Nobody joined — this lesson is unresolved and your credit is on hold" |'  VERSUS  06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:144 — '| Nobody joins a remote lesson | Grace elapses; **both-no-show** rule fires (D-03) — credit returns, no signal either side | Both: "Neither of you joined. Did this lesson move? Your credit is safe." |'  AND 06.01.03:268 — '| Q-03 | ~~Both-parties-no-show: who eats it?~~ **RESOLVED** → DT-09 / D-11. Nobody eats it: the credit returns...'  The same stale pointer is repeated at 06.01.04-lesson-delivery-session-record.md:246 — '| **Both parties no-show (remote)** | ... the ledger effect is 06.01.03's open Q-03 and is deliberately not decided here |'
findings.failure_scenario: Teacher and student both fail to join a remote Tuesday 17:00 lesson. An implementer building from 06.01.02 puts the credit in a `limbo` state, shows the student 'this lesson is unresolved and your credit is on hold', and waits for a rule that will never arrive because the question is closed. An implementer building from 06.01.03 returns the credit at grace expiry and shows 'your credit is safe'. The two builds differ in balance, in state machine, and in the user-visible message, on an event 06.01.03 DT-09 says is common enough to be a data-quality signal.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a both-no-show credit enters a limbo state or returns immediately, and what the student is told.

findings.claim: The refill-reversal behaviour (default ON) requires a burned credit to return and a teacher's already-accrued earning to unwind, but 06.01.02's credit lifecycle — presented as the exhaustive ledger state machine — has no transition out of `burned`, and no file allocates the reversed earning.
findings.evidence: 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:66-80 — '**Credit lifecycle** — the ledger's state machine. Every transition is an Audit Log event ...  reserved ──policy burn (06.01.03)─────> burned     [EARNING EVENT]' with no arrow leaving `burned`.  VERSUS 06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:41 — '| Refill reversal | On or off; **on by default** | If the vacated slot is refilled *and delivered*, the burn reverses (DT-08). |' and :154 — '| Student's slot is refilled and delivered after a late-cancel burn | Burn **auto-reverses** (DT-08). ... | Student: "Your slot was refilled — the credit you used has been returned."'  AND 06.01.03 D-12 (:254) — 'A burned credit **transfers its value to the teacher** as if the lesson were delivered'. 06.01.02's own cross-cut note to 06.01.03 (:270) lists only the burn/lapse distinction as 'New constraint from DT-04' and never mentions reversal.
findings.failure_scenario: Student late-cancels Tuesday; the burn fires, the teacher's payout accrues (06.01.03 D-12, 06.01.02 D-06). The teacher then refills that hour with a released one-off and delivers it, so refill reversal fires and the student's credit is returned. The teacher has now been paid twice for one hour and the ledger has no `burned → granted` edge to record it. One implementer claws back the accrued earning (unfairly, since the teacher taught the replacement), one lets the platform eat it, one refuses the reversal because the state machine forbids it. Nothing in the tree says which; 06.01.02 Q-04 covers chargeback loss allocation only.
findings.forcedInvention: The `burned → granted` ledger transition, and who absorbs the teacher's already-accrued earning when a refill reversal fires.

findings.claim: The delivery-mode enum has two incompatible definitions in the tree: four values including `academy` in the discovery/profile files, three values in the rate-card and cancellation-policy files that must price and govern it — while 06.01.04 D-15 makes an academy room one of only two legally acceptable configurations for a minor's in-person 1:1.
findings.evidence: 06.02-teacher-discovery-profiles-trials/06.02.03-teacher-discovery-match-criteria.md:63 — '| 4 | Mode | Yes | `remote` · `teacher's room` · `student's home` · `academy` — multi-select | Drives whether S5 contributes at all |' and 06.02.01-teacher-tuition-profile.md:29 — 'modes (remote / their room / student's home / academy)'.  VERSUS 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:28 — 'one line per (instrument × duration × mode × level), where duration ∈ {30, 45, 60, 90 min}, mode ∈ {remote, teacher's room, student's home}' and 06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:42 — '| Mode | Remote, teacher's room, or student's home | Policy is dimensioned per mode exactly as the rate card is (DT-11).'  AND 06.01.04-lesson-delivery-session-record.md:372 D-15 — 'A minor's in-person 1:1 requires a declared present adult **or** an academy room'.
findings.failure_scenario: A teacher on an academy roster ticks `academy` as a teaching mode on their profile; a parent filters teacher search on mode = `academy` (a hard filter per 06.02.03) and gets results. The teacher then opens the rate card to price it and no `academy` line can exist, because the mode enum has three values — so the lesson is unbookable (06.01.02 edge 18: 'the rate card is a hard precondition for the calendar'), and no cancellation policy can be dimensioned for it either. Worse, the one configuration 06.01.04 D-15 requires for a minor's in-person 1:1 that has no declared chaperone is the configuration the booking model cannot express. Two implementers split on whether `academy` is a distinct mode, an alias of `teacher's room`, or a room attribute — and each choice changes pricing, policy dimensioning and the safeguarding gate.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether `academy` is a fourth delivery mode (and therefore a rate-card and cancellation-policy dimension value) or a property of the `teacher's room` mode.

findings.claim: The series state named 'At Risk' has two different, incompatible entry conditions in the two files that own it — balance 0 in 06.01.01, available ≤ 2 or exhaustion-within-21-days in 06.01.02 — with no statement that they are two layers.
findings.evidence: 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.01-lesson-slot-booking-recurring-series.md:162 — '| **At Risk** | Balance 0, next occurrence unreserved | Student: amber series + "Top up by 30 Jul to keep Tuesday 17:00" with the exact release date. Teacher: "Amy's balance is empty — held until 30 Jul" |'  VERSUS 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:141 — 'When available credits reach **≤ 2**, or when reserved occurrences would exhaust the balance within **21 days** at the series' cadence — whichever fires first — the ledger raises an **at-risk** signal on the series and prompts a top-up.' and its States table :239 — '| At risk | Available ≤ 2, or reserved occurrences exhaust the balance within 21 days | "Your Tuesday slot is funded to 26 Aug — top up to keep it"'
findings.failure_scenario: A student holds 2 available credits on a weekly ongoing series. 06.01.02 says the series is At Risk and shows an amber top-up prompt; 06.01.01 says At Risk begins only at balance 0 and that entering it starts the 2-occurrence / 14-day grace clock that ends in Lapsed and a released standing slot. An implementer who unifies the two states starts the slot-release countdown while the student still has two paid lessons in hand. An implementer who keeps them separate must invent a second state name and a second copy set that neither file supplies.

findings.claim: The no-show grace formula is worked through on a lesson duration the rate-card enum cannot express, and under that enum both the min() and its stated floor are unreachable.
findings.evidence: 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.03-cancellation-makeup-no-show-policy.md:83 — '2. **At `scheduled_start + grace`** — the no-show evaluation. `grace = min(15 min, 50% × duration)`, floor 5 min. A 20-minute beginner's lesson gets 10 minutes, not 15.'  VERSUS 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:28 — 'duration ∈ {30, 45, 60, 90 min}'. (06.02.04-trial-lessons-conversion.md:22 also assumes a sub-30 duration: 'all staff offer a free 20-minute taster'.)
findings.failure_scenario: For every duration the rate card permits, 50% × duration ≥ 15, so grace is always exactly 15 minutes and both the min() and the 5-minute floor are dead code. An implementer either hard-codes 15 and silently drops the ability to sell the short beginner lessons the spec's own worked example and 06.02.04's academy taster policy assume exist, or extends the duration enum with values (20 min? 15 min?) nobody ratified — which then propagate into rate-card lines, credit fungibility (06.01.02 D-07) and slot buffers.

findings.claim: The package expiry floor as written rejects the term-fee billing shape that DT-07/D-09 identify as essential to the domain's cold-start supply, and the waiver that would rescue it is scoped to 'subscription-shaped packs', glossed in the body text as monthly grants only.
findings.evidence: 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:54 — 'Package expiry window ≥ `max(90 days, credits × 14 days)` and ≤ 24 months.'  AND :126 — 'The expiry floor above (`≥ 90 days`) is waived for subscription-shaped packs — a monthly grant is by construction a 1-month pack'.  VERSUS :253 DT-07 — 'a **term is a pack whose expiry is pinned to the Operator's term bound** ... the expiry floor must not block a 12-week term' and :120 — 'A **term fee** ... is a pack with `credits = weeks in term` and `expiry = the term bound the Operator publishes`'.
findings.failure_scenario: A UK academy publishes its autumn term as a pack: 12 credits, expiry pinned to the 18 December term bound, roughly 84 days out. Publish-time validation computes the floor as max(90, 12×14) = 168 days and blocks it with 'the shortest expiry for this pack is 168 days' — exactly the failure DT-07 says will mean 'academies ... will simply not be adopted'. One implementer reads D-09's 'waived for subscription-shaped packs' as covering both term and monthly and lets it through; another reads the body gloss ('a monthly grant is by construction a 1-month pack') as monthly-only and blocks it.

findings.claim: Free trials are the domain's primary acquisition mechanic and are modelled as a rate-card line, but the rate card's publish-time validation forbids a zero price.
findings.evidence: 06.02-teacher-discovery-profiles-trials/06.02.04-trial-lessons-conversion.md:20 — '**As Teacher**: chooses whether to offer trials and at what price (free / reduced / full)' and :22 — 'sets a house trial policy (all staff offer a free 20-minute taster)'.  VERSUS 06.01-lesson-booking-packages-delivery/06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:273 — 'a **trial is not a credit**: it is a rate-card line of its own (often free or reduced) drawing against no pack' and :51 — 'Publish-time validation (all fail closed, all with the offending value echoed back): - List price > 0, and within the Operator's floor/ceiling'.
findings.failure_scenario: A teacher sets a free 30-minute trial. If the trial really is 'a rate-card line of its own', publish validation rejects it with 'List price > 0' and the free trial — the mechanic 06.02.04 D-02, 06.02 CX-04 and domain CX-01 all build the funnel on — cannot be published. An implementer must invent either a price-0 exemption on the trial line, a separate trial object outside the rate card, or a floor-price trial. The rate card's stated dimensions (instrument × duration × mode × level) also carry no trial axis, so where the line lives is undefined.

findings.claim: The level hard filter is specified as '±1 band' against a band scale the file's own Deep Think argues cannot exist, and that scale is enumerated nowhere — while the sibling age bands are enumerated precisely.

VERSUS DT-04 at :241 — '"Intermediate" is not commensurable across instruments or traditions ... never as a point value on a shared scale that does not exist.'  Contrast the age bands, fully enumerated at :61 — '`under-11` · `11–17` · `18–24` · `25–64` · `65+`'. S3's facet key at :93 is 'Per `(instrument, level band, age band)`'.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must instantiate the level bands to compute `[stated−1, stated+1]`, to define the teacher's 'accepted level range', and to key S3's per-facet conversion counter. Another keeps the proxy-fact profile with no bands, at which point '±1 band' is uncomputable and S3's facet key has no second component. The two produce different result pools for the same query.

One implementer redistributes S5's 10 points proportionally across S2–S8 by analogy with the stated S1 rule; another leaves them unallocated so every remote result tops out at 90. The two produce different orderings whenever two candidates differ mainly on reviews or page completeness, and the teacher-facing 'where each input is costing them' view (Role Lens, :28) reports different deficits for the same teacher depending on which build they are looking at — on a number D-10 commits to publishing precisely so it can be interrogated.

Neither file cites the other on this point, and neither supplies the declaration/consent mechanism that 06.01.04's own reasoning requires.

The Operator role grants occupancy and attendance, never content, at any tier. A standing silent content read over a child's lesson would make the platform the threat.'  VERSUS 06.03-curriculum-assignments-practice/06.03.02-assignments-submissions-timestamped-feedback.md:29 — '| Operator | Read-only | As an academy: reads assignments, submissions and feedback for **teachers on their roster** ... to quality-assure their staff. A submission is a minor's recording of themselves: :44 — 'A submission is audio or video — **declared by the assignment**' and D-13 at :201 defaults technique instruments to video. 06.03.02's own D-10 (:198) forbids the teacher forwarding the same artifact: 'A child's recording leaving the relationship it was made in is a safeguarding failure regardless of intent.'
findings.failure_scenario: A 10-year-old submits a video of their fretting hand to their academy teacher. Under 06.03.02 the academy head can open and watch it at any time, silently and retrospectively, and can still do so after the teacher leaves — the precise shape 06.01.04 D-13 rejects as 'a standing silent content read over a child's lesson'. One implementer builds the QA read as a plain Operator role permission per 06.03.02; another refuses it per D-13's 'never content, at any tier' and forces the declared per-occurrence pattern. Neither file says whether the student or guardian is told the academy can read the exchange — 06.03.02 edge 26 covers only the guardian's own visibility.

findings.failure_scenario: A well-known producer offers 2 mentorship places (D-03: capacity 1–3) and receives 200 applications. Whether the platform caps applications, closes the listing when full, or lets all 200 through is undecided and unowned — and the file itself calls the uncapped outcome 'a bad experience for 200 people'. Separately, the `Lapsed` state exists in the States table with no defined rendering: one implementer surfaces a nudge (which DT-02 argues drives mentors off the platform), another lets it die silently (which leaves the mentee with no signal). No stage is scheduled to rule on either.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether mentor application caps exist; and what the Lapsed state renders.

findings.claim: 06.08's Happy Path specifies automatic certificate issuance on completion; the same file's Cross-Cut Notes, 06.04's CX and the domain CX all record automatic issuance as rejected. The one survivor D-02 contemplates therefore has no defined issuance trigger.
findings.evidence: 06.08-certificates-badges-verification.md:50 — '2. Certificate issues **automatically** in the author's or academy's name'.  VERSUS the same file :86 — 'Touches **06.04.03 Course Consumption** — the completion trigger. Note 06.04 CX R-04 already rejected auto-issuance.'; 06.04-course-marketplace-authoring-cx.md:152 R-04 — 'Considered auto-issuing a certificate on completion — the LMS default. **Rejected** at breadth on demand grounds'; education-lessons-mentorship-cx.md:257 — 'Trigger chain: Completion → issuance is **rejected as automatic** (`06.04-...-cx.md#R-04`).'
findings.failure_scenario: 06.08 D-02 keeps one survivor — 'the academy-issued certificate for children' — alive as the only case with real demand. An implementer building it has a Happy Path saying issuance is automatic and three other artifacts saying automatic issuance was rejected, with no manual trigger specified anywhere (no Operator action, no term-end hook, no approval step of the kind 06.03.05 D-02 mandates for reports). The whole feature is banded `wont` in the ledger, which limits the blast radius, but the contradiction is unmarked on the Happy Path side.

findings.claim: The domain's success-measure question is closed on the finding that exactly one measure exists — an exam-board grade — and the feature that supplies it is separately decided to be absent in the ratified primary market. The consequence, that the domain has no working success measure where it will actually launch, is stated nowhere and tracked by no open row.
findings.evidence: education-lessons-mentorship-index.md:127 — '| Q-08 | ~~Does the domain have any success metric it can measure?~~ **RESOLVED — exactly one, and the platform does not own it: an exam-board grade.** ... | User | Closed |'.  VERSUS 06.09-exam-board-alignment.md:107 D-03 — 'The feature is **absent**, not empty, for teachers who don't use grades | Most of the world, and nearly all of the US.' and its Q-01 resolution at :115 — 'the market priority has since been decided by the owner: the US ... **D-32** ... So: no board is required for the primary market'.  Q-08's own residual pointer sends the reader to 'the measure exists only where the graded tradition does (06.09 D-03, 06.09 Q-01 at MoSCoW)' — but 06.09 Q-01 is now Closed, so the pointer terminates without carrying the gap forward.
findings.failure_scenario: A PRD author reads Q-08 as closed and takes the exam grade as the domain's progress measure, then discovers at 06.09 D-03 that the feature renders nothing at all for nearly every US teacher — and D-32 makes the US the launch market. The domain's other three progress candidates were each rejected as unmeasurable (06.03.05 DT-02, 06.04.03 DT-02, 06.08 DT-02), so in the primary market the domain has zero measurable success criteria, no metric with a number, a unit or a timeframe anywhere in its index, and no open row assigned to anyone to notice.

findings.claim: Four cross-cut seams in the domain CX carry role scoping marked [PENDING] with no owner — two against a stage the same tree records as completed, two with no target at all.
findings.evidence: education-lessons-mentorship-cx.md:231 — '### CX-08: Learning Paths ↔ Course Marketplace ... **Role scoping**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5]`, pending 06.07 Q-01'; :274 — '### CX-10: Mentorship ↔ Teacher Discovery ... **Role scoping**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5]`, pending 06.06 Q-01'; :287 — '### CX-11 ... **Role scoping**: `[PENDING]`.'; :302 — '### CX-12 ... **Role scoping**: `[PENDING]`.'  The same index that owns this CX documents Step 5 as finished — education-lessons-mentorship-index.md:123, 'Deferral target re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5 run' — and re-points its own rows accordingly; these four were not re-pointed.
findings.failure_scenario: CX-11 (a recorded masterclass is a course) and CX-12 (exam boards as a discovery filter) each describe an object crossing a feature boundary with real access consequences — who may sell a recorded masterclass, who may filter on a board — and both hold their role scoping at a bare [PENDING] with nobody assigned and no stage named. Unlike the file's other deferrals, there is nothing to follow: a downstream spec writer either invents the role scoping or ships the seam unscoped.
